description: §17 Worked Example 5 (invalid) verbatim — a second `<span else>` tries to extend a chain that already terminated at `else`, firing E-CTRL-003. CASCADE NOTE: E-CTRL-001 co-fires by design — `collapseIfChains` breaks out of the chain scan at the E-CTRL-003 fire (ast-builder.js:17598-17603), so the outer loop re-visits the trailing `<span else>` as a now-orphaned `else` and additionally reports E-CTRL-001. Both are real diagnostics on the same element; `codes` is a superset check so only E-CTRL-003 is asserted here (E-CTRL-001 is pinned by its own case). W-PROGRAM-SPA-INFERRED co-fires incidentally at severity info.
rationale: §17.1.1 Normative Rules: an `else` element SHALL be the terminal element of its chain. No element carrying `if=`, `else-if=`, or `else` SHALL appear immediately after an `else` element at the same parent level as part of the same chain. The compiler SHALL reject any element that would extend a chain past an `else` (E-CTRL-003). §17 Error Code Summary + §34 both register E-CTRL-003 at severity Error. S478 (bootstrap triage C7 / F2): migrated to a twinnable declaration. The legacy inline-typed state-object opener `<session { … }` only declared the cell(s) the chain reads; it is now the legacy declaration `<isAdmin>: bool = false`, which the `scrml fix` §66 rules twin to a §66 declaration (§66.21 row 1). (A direct §66 `let <x:T=v/>` here makes impl#1's ESM client emit throw — "The keyword 'let' is reserved" — so the twinnable legacy declaration keeps both implementations graded.) The if= / else-if= / else chain under test is unchanged.
